articleTitle: Multivariable modelling for building energy management
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Modelling and Simulation for Thermal Management (Digest No. 1997/043)
abstract: Preliminary results from an exercise aimed at developing models to assist in the operation of Building Energy Management systems are presented. The models developed are used to predict temperature and humidity over different horizons for possible use in different applications.

articleTitle: The simulation and measurement of the temperature rise in a power semiconductor device under transient conditions
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Modelling and Simulation for Thermal Management (Digest No. 1997/043)
abstract: This paper first examines the method widely used by semiconductor manufacturers to generate the transient thermal response curves. It then goes on to examine the validity of such curves by means of measuring the die temperature rise under pulsed power conditions using an infrared camera and by generating a comprehensive thermal model of the semiconductor device and package. The results are finally presented and conclusions are made.

articleTitle: Modelling heat dissipation in dc-dc converters
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Modelling and Simulation for Thermal Management (Digest No. 1997/043)
abstract: The modelling of heat dissipation from heat generating components through the device as a whole is fundamental to the future design of DC-DC converters. Simulation of device thermal performance prior to manufacture will enable rapid evaluation of material or component changes, and thus help to reduce the product development time. A 3-dimensional TLM based model of thermal diffusion within the component has, therefore, been constructed. Here we describe the "first generation" model of the thermal system and present the results of some preliminary simulations.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Modelling and Simulation for Thermal Management (Digest No. 1997/043)
abstract: As computing power increases there is a natural tendency to use it to tackle larger problems in greater detail. The perfect description of a semiconductor device may provide an exact measure of the power dissipation. But when it is realised that the chip is on a header, encapsulated in a package which is attached to one of many circuit boards within a cabinet, etc., then it is time to stand back and look at the forest and ignore the stomata on the leaves on the trees. This paper provides a tour of the problem, highlights some recent developments and suggests areas which might be usefully investigated in the future.

articleTitle: Temperature estimation of semiconductor die heating using numerical techniques in real time
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Modelling and Simulation for Thermal Management (Digest No. 1997/043)
abstract: This paper first details many of the practical difficulties associated with the temperature measurement of a power semiconductor die housed within a commercial package. The paper then goes on to describe a method of protection which is based on predicting the die temperature in real time by the use of a numerical model continuously calculated on a low cost microprocessor.
